title: Envelope
description:
The outermost wire frame for every message on the bus. `seq` is monotonic per connection and is the ordering / resync key; `at` is when the frame was created; `body` is the payload, discriminated by direction. This document defines the contract only; the bus is a transport and this repository owns neither the traffic nor the producers.

What is modelled here is the *wire*: the bytes a producer emits and a client reads. Daemon-internal actor and host types are deliberately out of scope — the cut is at the transport boundary.

Two conventions hold throughout, and both are load-bearing:

1. **Unknown properties are ignored, never rejected.** No object in this schema sets `additionalProperties: false`, because the reference producer's deserializer ignores fields it does not know. A schema that rejected them would refuse documents the bus itself accepts, which is the wrong direction for a contract that must tolerate a newer peer. The `extra-fields` fixture pins this.

2. **A property is `required` exactly when the producer always writes it.** A nullable-but-required property (`name`, `tool`, `note`, `agents`, `resume`, `gap`) is one the producer emits as `null` rather than omitting; an *absent* property (`trace`, `parent_span_id`) is one the producer genuinely leaves off the wire. The distinction is not cosmetic: code generated from this schema drops unrequired properties when it re-emits, so mislabelling one would make a generated client emit documents no producer ever produces. Read-side leniency (the producer also accepts a missing `name`) is deserializer tolerance, not the wire contract.

seq.description: Monotonic sequence number, per connection. Ordering and resync key: delivery is best-effort, so a client that sees a gap asks for a snapshot rather than assuming loss.

at.description: Unix epoch milliseconds when the envelope was created. Stamped by the bus, never by the producer — a producer's own timestamp, where one exists, rides inside the payload as provenance (see `CurationProposed.ts`).

Body.title: Body
Body.description: The payload, discriminated by direction of travel. `Event` is bus to client; `Command` is client to bus.

BusEvent.title: BusEvent
BusEvent.description: A single typed event emitted to subscribed clients. Every event names a subject — the cross-plane join key — so events from different planes about the same entity line up on one timeline.

trace.description: Cross-plane trace context. Absent means untraced, and an untraced event is byte-identical to one from before tracing existed — which is why this property is omitted rather than written as null. Producers propagate the context they were given, or mint one only at a true origin.

TraceContext.title: TraceContext
TraceContext.description:
Trace context for one event, aligned with the W3C `traceparent` field shapes. `trace_id` is the correlation key for a whole causal chain and is propagated unchanged; `span_id` identifies this event's span; `parent_span_id` links to the causing event's span.

This is the one place the schema is deliberately *stricter* than the producer's own type, which carries these as unvalidated strings. The boundary that accepts producer-supplied contexts checks this shape and rejects a malformed one rather than propagating it to every subscriber, so the hex shape is genuinely part of the wire contract and not merely a convention. The all-zero value is excluded because `traceparent` defines it as invalid.

parent_span_id.description: The causing event's span. Absent at the root of a chain; omitted rather than null, so a root context is byte-identical to a context from a producer that does not parent its events.

Attention.title: Attention
Attention.description: Urgency signal carried by every event. Drives the operator's badge and anything that pushes notifications; gates default to `NeedsYou`. `Normal` means no operator action; `NeedsYou` means look when convenient (also used for a surfaced error that is not a gate); `Urgent` means act now.

SubjectRef.title: SubjectRef
SubjectRef.description: What an event is about — the single identity join key across planes. The same agent or factory id is stamped by every plane, so their timelines reconcile without a translation table.

EventKind.title: EventKind
EventKind.description:
The event payload. Deliberately a small, coarse set of per-plane verbs: fine-grained variety rides in plane-owned open-vocabulary string fields rather than in new kinds, which is what keeps this enumeration from sprawling.

Adding a kind is an additive, minor change; a consumer that meets an unknown kind is meeting a newer peer, and should say so rather than guess. Note that a plane owning a vocabulary field means the bus transports its values without interpreting them — `verdict`, `outcome`, `deviation_kind`, `proposed_scope` and `source_trust` are all strings for that reason, not because their values are arbitrary.

data.description: An agent process started.

name.description: The agent's recognizable name, if one was assigned at spawn. Echoed here so a client can label the agent without a second query. Null when unnamed, in which case clients display the id.

data.description: The agent process exited.

The tool the agent is now running changed — the decoration behind a `working — <tool>` label. Content-free by contract: the tool's *name* is a safe category, its input never rides the bus. Separate from `AgentStatus` on purpose, because the status is asserted independently by another signal and folding the two together would let them fight over the label.

tool.description: The current tool, or null between tools.

data.description: An operator resolved an open gate.
A mail message arrived — a hint to re-query the durable store, never the message itself. Durable things live in their own store; bus notifications about them are doorbells.

The memory plane injected items into an agent's context. Content-free by construction: ids, scores, and a short reason — never the fact text or the query that retrieved it. The carrying event's subject names the agent the injection went to.

items.description: The injected item ids — opaque refs into the owning plane's store.

scores.description: Ranker scores, parallel-length to `items`. The parallel-length rule is enforced by the ingress that accepts these, not by this schema: JSON Schema cannot relate two array lengths, and a contract that silently fails to check a rule it appears to state is worse than one that does not state it.

reason.description: Short, content-free reason — which ranker and cut produced this.

data.description: The memory plane's curator proposed a promotion and opened a curation gate. Content-free: hex refs and vocabulary strings, never fact text. The carrying event's subject is the gate.

content_hash.description: Content hash of the proposed fact — a content-free ref, in practice sha256 hex. Not pattern-constrained here: the producer's own field is a plain string, and a schema stricter than the producer would reject documents the bus accepts.

proposed_scope.description: Proposed promotion scope. An open vocabulary owned by the memory plane; new values arrive without a schema change.

source_trust.description: Provenance trust level. An open vocabulary owned by the memory plane.

ts.description: Producer-side timestamp, as provenance. Distinct from the envelope's `at`, which is when the bus broadcast the frame. Not `format`-constrained, for the same superset reason as `content_hash`.

data.description: The owning plane voided a curation gate — for instance because the content drifted before it could be applied. A doorbell, not an authority: a consumer verifies against the owning plane's store before acting on it. Void is terminal and absorbing, so answered-then-voided is a legitimate sequence rather than a conflict.
A workflow run started.
The workflow entered a phase, possibly as a retry of it.
A phase evaluation rendered its verdict — never the raw output it judged.

verdict.description: The evaluator's verdict. An open vocabulary owned by the orchestration plane.

gap.description: Optional numeric gap score behind the verdict.

flags.description: Content-free flag labels attached by the evaluator.

data.description: The run deviated from its plan in a logged, non-fatal way.

deviation_kind.description: The deviation category. An open vocabulary owned by the orchestration plane.

data.description: A parallel region fanned out. Leg events parent to this event's span, which is the concurrent-fan-out ambiguity the span tree exists to resolve.
One leg of a parallel region finished.

leg.description: The leg's 0-based index within its region.

outcome.description: The leg outcome. An open vocabulary owned by the orchestration plane.

data.description: The workflow run failed terminally.

AgentStatus.title: AgentStatus
AgentStatus.description: The observable lifecycle state of an agent — exactly one at a time. `Fresh` is the spawn state, left only by the first real prompt, so a never-driven agent reads differently from one that finished a turn. `UnsentDraft` is the state that earns its own name: the operator typed a prompt and never submitted it, so nothing is running while it looks as though something is. `Unknown` means no signal, not an error.

AgentRole.title: AgentRole
AgentRole.description: The agent's position in the agent tree. Only `Solo` is emitted today; `Lead` and `Teammate` are reserved so the tree work lands additively rather than as a wire change.

SpawnOrigin.title: SpawnOrigin
SpawnOrigin.description: Where a spawn request came from. Only `Operator` is emitted today; the rest are reserved.

source.description: A string identifying the external trigger.

AgentView.title: AgentView
AgentView.description: The optional view tier, delivered only to clients that opt into it. This is the single exception to the rule that payloads carry refs and never content: the live terminal is the one thing an observer cannot reconstruct from ids.

oneOf.description: DEPRECATED since 0.1.1: producers no longer emit it. Use `Grid` (and the `RequestFull` command for a one-shot full frame). Still accepted; removed at the next breaking release.

A damage delta of the agent's screen. Per connection and agent, the first `Grid` frame is always a full frame (`reset: true`); an incremental's `epoch` exceeds the previous frame's, while a reshipped full frame may repeat it.

data.description: A `gridwire::GridDelta`, opaque to this schema: decode it with the `gridwire` crate's own `GridDelta` type. Its serde shape is gridwire's, verbatim; the envelope carries it without re-describing it, so the two cannot drift apart.

oneOf.description: A semantic terminal event: title, bell, clipboard write, shell-integration mark, search result. Ordered and never coalesced.

data.description: A `gridwire::BackendEvent`, opaque to this schema: decode it with the `gridwire` crate's own `BackendEvent` type. Its serde shape is gridwire's, verbatim; the envelope carries it without re-describing it, so the two cannot drift apart. A unit variant serializes as a bare string (`"Bell"`), the others as a one-key object (`{"Title": "..."}`).

ScreenSnapshot.title: ScreenSnapshot
ScreenSnapshot.description: A snapshot of a terminal grid. Row-major: the cell at (row, col) is `cells[row * cols + col]`. That `cells` has exactly `rows * cols` entries is a producer invariant this schema cannot state — JSON Schema cannot relate an array's length to two sibling integers — so a consumer that indexes blind on a short buffer is a consumer bug, not a schema gap. DEPRECATED since 0.1.1 with `AgentView::Terminal`; removed at the next breaking release.

Cell.title: Cell
Cell.description: One terminal cell. DEPRECATED since 0.1.1 with `AgentView::Terminal`; removed at the next breaking release.

ch.description:
Exactly one Unicode scalar value.

Deliberately *not* length-constrained, and the reason is a cross-language trap worth stating: JSON Schema's `minLength`/`maxLength` count characters, but implementations disagree on what a character is — a validator over UTF-16 counts an astral scalar such as an emoji as two, while one over code points counts it as one. A `maxLength: 1` here would therefore accept the same document in one language and reject it in another, which is precisely the divergence this repository's corpus exists to prevent. The single-scalar rule is enforced by the producer's own character type instead.

Color.title: Color
Color.description: A cell colour: the terminal default, a palette index, or a 24-bit truecolour. `Default` defers to the renderer's theme rather than naming a colour, which is what lets one grid render correctly under light and dark themes. DEPRECATED since 0.1.1 with `AgentView::Terminal`, its only user (through `Cell`); removed at the next breaking release. It carries no `deprecated` keyword itself: on a union the Python generator puts the flag on the model's own root field, which pydantic cannot then read, and the deprecation already reaches it through `Cell` and `ScreenSnapshot`.

Indexed.description: A 256-colour palette index; 0 through 15 are the ANSI colours.

StructuredTurn.title: StructuredTurn
StructuredTurn.description: A structured transcript turn. Reserved and deliberately minimal — it lands properly with the transcript path that will produce it, on the principle that a kind is cut against a real emitter's bytes rather than guessed ahead of one.

role.description: The conversational role of this turn.

summary.description: A short, content-free summary — never raw output.

Gate.title: Gate
Gate.description:
A pending operator decision that blocks something. One primitive for every moment a human is needed — a tool permission, an agent's question, a memory promotion, a workflow approval — which is why a client only ever implements one answering path.

`producer` and `subject_ref` both appear and neither is redundant: `producer` routes the presentation and the handler, `subject_ref` is where the operator jumps to.

options.description: Ordered choices the operator may select. Empty for an open-answer gate — a client must therefore offer free text and escalation even when this list is empty, rather than rendering an empty button row.

context_summary.description: A brief human-readable summary of why the human is needed — never raw content.

GateProducer.title: GateProducer
GateProducer.description: The category of subsystem that opened a gate.

GateOption.title: GateOption
GateOption.description: One selectable choice within a gate.

id.description: Machine-stable identifier, echoed back in a `Select` resolution.

label.description: Human-readable text shown to the operator.

GateResolution.title: GateResolution
GateResolution.description: How an operator resolved a gate. Three modes, always all three: a preset option, free text, or escalating to a live conversation. `Chat` resolves by the interaction itself rather than by a payload — for an agent gate the operator is dropped into the session, so there is nothing to carry.

note.description: Optional free-text note accompanying the selection.

BusCommand.title: BusCommand
BusCommand.description: A command sent from a client to the bus.

data.description: Subscribe to events, with an optional agent filter and a capability grant.

agents.description: Restrict to events about these agents. Null means no agent filter — distinct from an empty list, which filters everything out.

data.description: Spawn a new agent process.

cwd.description: Working directory for the spawned process.

resume.description: Resume an existing session rather than starting fresh. Null starts a new one.

name.description: An optional recognizable name for the agent, shown instead of the bare id. Null leaves it unnamed.

data.description: Write raw bytes to an agent's terminal — the keystream path, for interactive typing and menu navigation.

bytes.description: The raw bytes to write, as octets.

data.description:
Type one line at the agent's prompt and submit it.

This is not expressible as `SendInput` with a trailing newline, which is why it is its own command rather than a convenience: a terminator inside a single text burst is absorbed into the prompt's draft instead of submitting it, so submitting requires the host to split the write. Raw keystreams stay on `SendInput`.

text.description: The line to type and submit, with no trailing newline.

data.description: Switch the client's focused agent.

Declare this connection's viewport for an agent. A declaration, not a command: the agent's terminal takes the smallest viewport declared across live connections, per dimension, or the producer's default when none is. A declaration lives while the agent is in the declaring connection's view subscription; it lapses on hang-up, on a `Subscribe` that drops the agent, or on one without `caps.view`. Wire shape unchanged since 0.1.0; only its arbitration changed.
Resolve an open gate. The one command that answers a permission prompt, a question, a memory promotion or a workflow gate — by id, in any of the three resolution modes.
Send a lightweight nudge. Deliberately not durable — a nudge that must survive the recipient going away is mail.
Reship the agent's current screen to THIS connection as one full `Grid` frame, answered on the asking connection's stream in order with the deltas that follow.

Declare whether this connection's viewer has the agent focused. Aggregated like `Resize`: the agent counts as focused while any live viewer says so, and the producer reports a change to the application only if it enabled focus reporting.

Terminate the agent: the producer forgets its recovery record, then kills it, so it is never resumed. The only way to end an agent; closing or dropping a connection only detaches. Guarding against an accidental quit is the client's job.
Scroll the agent's shared display through its history; every viewer sees it. A no-op while the application is on the alternate screen. Accepted only from a connection viewing the agent.

amount.description: A `gridwire::ScrollAmount`, opaque to this schema: decode it with the `gridwire` crate's own `ScrollAmount` type. Its serde shape is gridwire's, verbatim; the envelope carries it without re-describing it, so the two cannot drift apart. A unit variant serializes as a bare string (`"PageUp"`), the others as a one-key object (`{"Lines": -3}`).

data.description: Put the agent's previous (negative) or next (positive) shell-integration mark at the top of its shared display. Accepted only from a connection viewing the agent.

Search the agent's history and screen for a regex and bring the match into view. The answer is a `SearchResult` event to every viewer; a client applies only a result it is awaiting. Accepted only from a connection viewing the agent.

Target.title: Target
Target.description: Where a command or message is delivered. Only `One` is implemented today; the rest are reserved so multicast lands without a wire change.

Caps.title: Caps
Caps.description: The capability grant negotiated at subscription time. `status` is the universal floor — every transport gets status and commands, including one too small to render a terminal. `view` opts into the heavy live-terminal tier, which is why it is a grant rather than an assumption.

KindClass.title: KindClass
KindClass.description: A coarse category of event kinds, used for subscription filtering. `Curation` is separate from `Memory` on purpose: curation gates are the integrity-sensitive ones, and the class boundary is where that capability seam falls.

KindFilter.title: KindFilter
KindFilter.description: A subscription filter over kind classes.

classes.description: The classes to subscribe to. An empty list means *all* classes, not none — the common case is an unfiltered subscription, and making that the empty value keeps a client from having to enumerate a list that grows.

MailDraft.title: MailDraft
MailDraft.description: A message composed by a sender, ready to submit. The delivered, durable record lives in the mail store; this is only what goes over the wire to create one.

AgentRef.title: AgentRef
AgentRef.description:
An agent's vendor-neutral id, and the join key every plane stamps.

Deliberately unconstrained. The producer's own type is an unvalidated string, so any pattern here would be a schema that rejects ids the bus accepts — the same superset rule the registry schema states from the other direction, where a *key* pattern must stay a superset of every id the bus accepts.

SessionId.title: SessionId
SessionId.description: The hosted session's own id, used to resume it. Distinct from `AgentRef`: one names the agent to every plane, the other is the vendor's handle for its conversation.

FactoryRef.title: FactoryRef
FactoryRef.description: Identifies an agent factory — a spawn template and the project scope around it.

GroupRef.title: GroupRef
GroupRef.description: Identifies an operator-named set of agents.

MemoryItemRef.title: MemoryItemRef
MemoryItemRef.description: Identifies a memory item — an opaque ref into the owning plane's store, never the item itself.

MailId.title: MailId
MailId.description: Identifies a message in the durable mail store. An integer, unlike every other id here, because the mail store assigns it.

TraceId.title: TraceId
TraceId.description: A trace id: 32 lowercase hex characters, not all zero. Propagate it unchanged along a causal chain; mint one only where a chain truly begins.

SpanId.title: SpanId
SpanId.description: A span id: 16 lowercase hex characters, not all zero.
